description: The open-web search log records 18 native search actions, 72 query terms, and 433 ordered result headers. This does not reproduce the original LexisNexis/source universe, and result counts cannot establish that no other protest occurred.
required_followup: Compare with the original search protocol and accessible systematic news archives if available; retain this as an open-web first pass.

description: Searches included English, Kinyarwanda, French and a limited Swahili-term check. The MUHAZI YACU article was read in Kinyarwanda, but interpretation has not received independent linguistic review; other-language/local indexing may be incomplete.
required_followup: Have the relevant Kinyarwanda passages independently reviewed and document additional language/archive coverage before eligibility review.

description: Queries included local Gatsibo/Gakoni and Kigali terms, official and rights-report domains, national news, and student, labor, transport, health, teacher, farmer/vendor and land topics. They do not amount to systematic district-by-district or sector-by-sector coverage; most event-specific evidence concerns Gakoni.
required_followup: Extend local/regional and official-source checks across Rwanda’s districts and document which sectors and regions were actually searched; do not infer national absence from this batch.

description: The official current MM dataset, universe, additional Coding Procedure and compatibility gate remain unresolved at the project level.
required_followup: Coordinator must complete the official-baseline and protocol review before any export or official eligibility claim.

description: No simultaneous protest-attendance estimate is reported. The “all students” wording, 16 arrests, enrollment of 372 (including 288 refugees), and the “15 students” photo caption do not establish a count at the protest. Public-meeting character and the 50-person threshold remain unknown.
required_followup: Seek direct event-specific attendance evidence and verify that at least 50 people participated in a public meeting before considering inclusion.

description: The student account describes a condition that a peer be released and returned before students resume classes, while KT Press frames the strike against a suspension. Neither opened report clearly establishes whether protesters directed a demand to school management, local police or another competent Rwanda state authority, or government policy. No listed demand category clearly maps to the school-level condition.
required_followup: Verify the exact stated demand and its recipient, including whether it was directed to a competent state authority such as local police or to government policy, from direct contemporaneous reporting or records; retain the candidate as pending evidence until then.

description: The trigger accounts differ: KT Press attributes the suspension to repeated dormitory departures to drink; MUHAZI YACU reports different alleged conduct and a COVID-rules briefing. Both cite Mayor Richard Gasana, leaving a shared official-source dependency and unresolved account conflict.
required_followup: Look for original student/school/police/official statements or an independent contemporary account; preserve both reports and do not resolve by outlet count.

description: KT Press dates the strike to 7 February; the reports separately describe class refusal on 8 February and closure on 9 February. The 26 February reopening report is a later response, not an event end. The physical end of protest activity and whether the refusal was continuous remain unknown.
required_followup: Find an event-specific source for the physical end and distinguish strike, later class refusal, school closure and ministerial response.

description: S001 and S002 are separately published local reports, but both cite the same mayor and disagree on the trigger. S006 is the same KT Press publisher/byline as S001 and repeats event details; it adds a ministerial response but is not independent event corroboration.
required_followup: Search for an original or independent event-specific account; do not count S006 as an independent confirmation or equate separate outlets with fully independent origins.

description: The reports support arrests (16 students); accommodation, beatings, crowd dispersal, ignore, killings and shootings remain unknown. Student-reported protester property damage is coded yes, but is not independently corroborated. No silence is coded as explicit absence.
required_followup: Check event-specific sources for each response dimension separately; do not infer dispersal, beatings or state accommodation from arrests, school closure or later reopening.

description: The exact UNHCR February operational-update PDF URL passed the saved gate/manual process, but the web tool returned Internal Error and said the URL was inaccessible via the tool. No HTTP status or publisher-origin denial was exposed and no PDF content was retrieved.
required_followup: Preserve as technically inaccessible with unknown HTTP; any later attempt requires a fresh authorized phase and exact-URL gate. Do not retry or use an alternate URL under this record.

description: The exact Kigali Today URL represented by S003 matches January source RW202101-S006, whose body was already opened in the January dossier. S003 is prior-unit-only here and is not a new February read or corroboration.
required_followup: Use the saved January record only as prior-unit context; do not repeat the body request. Preserve February source evidence independently.

description: Search-title leads name Brussels, Paris, Geneva, The Hague, Lyon (S011–S013) and a separate embassy demonstration in Kinshasa (S014), all outside Rwanda. They are kept separate from the domestic Gakoni candidate; their bodies, dates, turnout and demands were not reviewed. S011–S013 may be related/reprinted, but relationship and independence are unverified.
required_followup: If a separate diaspora/foreign-territory study is in scope, verify each city/action independently and trace Jambo News republication/origin; do not aggregate with Rwanda-territory attendance.

description: S009’s title describes support for Yvonne Idamange, S010 is a security alert, and S015 is a march against a Rwandan ambassador; title-only evidence does not establish location, an executed gathering, country target, turnout or relationship among them.
required_followup: Keep as separate context/search leads unless later authorized body review establishes a specific event, location and relevant demand.

description: S021 and S022 are taxi/taxi-moto protest search titles; body, exact date, sector, relation to one another and any continuation of January’s unresolved metering lead are unknown. No prior-month continuation is established for this unit.
required_followup: If these leads are revisited in an authorized phase, establish the event date and identity before linking to January or treating them as February continuations.
